positive: The official Requirements adapter exposes a read-only existing-run contract resolver that takes a project root and run ID, calls the package-owned frozen binding resolver, and derives every required Requirements rule reference from that validated immutable pack.

The adapter accepts bundled-v2 ready resolution and bounded legacy-v1 read-only resolution as distinct compatibility modes, with legacy attempted only when the bundled binding is categorically missing.
Every returned rule path remains inside the validated resolved pack, exists as a regular non-symlink file, and contains its required official marker.
Selector changes, process working-directory changes, and caller-provided compatibility manifest values cannot affect the new existing-run resolver.
The existing pre-run stage_contract and public stage_request behavior remain unchanged for Phase 3 to migrate after provisioning and binding are wired.
The exact targeted proof collects four frozen-adapter scenarios: three currently fail only because the new API is absent, while the existing public-route preservation scenario already passes.
negative: Phase 2B.2 does not wire the new resolver into stage_request, task-start, Planning Lock, MCP, or any host projection and does not change the legacy public route before Phase 3 can create a frozen binding.

The new resolver never reads current.json, resolves relative to process cwd, accepts a caller manifest path, contacts the network, executes pack content, writes project state, provisions a pack, or creates or rewrites a run binding.

Missing, altered, stale, incompatible, conflicting, legacy-unauthorized, or unsafe state fails closed without falling back to another pack; only a categorically missing bundled binding may attempt bounded legacy continuation.
The approved proof command excludes the two unrelated whole-module activation failures and cannot be broadened without a new approved proof boundary.
This slice does not edit tailtrail/aidlc_bundle.py, scripts/aidlc-official-bridge.py, scripts/planning_lock.py, scripts/task-start.py, schemas, package registration, CLI dispatch, or documentation.
